name: Horde
strategy: Use large formations, overlapping engagements, and numerical superiority.
qualificationNote: A formation containing four or more surviving Models qualifies for the standard numerical requirements of this doctrine.

commands.name: Endless Ranks
commands.effect: If the active Unit has at least four surviving Models, it counts as one additional Unit for objective control until the end of the Round.

commands.name: Massed Volley
commands.effect: If the active Unit has at least four surviving Models, its next ranged Attack this Assault Phase gains +2 Attack dice. If another friendly Unit with at least four surviving Models is within Short, also gain Accurate 1 on that Attack.

commands.name: Mob Tactics
commands.effect: The active Unit gains Anti-Infantry 4 on its next Melee Attack against an Infantry enemy also Engaged by a different friendly Unit with at least four surviving Models.

commands.name: Pack Coordination
commands.effect: When a friendly Unit within Short of another friendly Unit with at least four surviving Models is attacked, it gains Tough 2 against that Attack.

commands.name: Encirclement
commands.effect: When the active Unit attacks an enemy also Engaged by a different friendly Unit with at least four surviving Models, that enemy worsens Evade by one step against this Attack.

doctrineIdentity: Numerical advantage and coordinated formations. Standard generic Line Infantry and Ranged Infantry qualify without reinforcement. Larger hordes remain more reliable because they retain their model-count requirements after suffering casualties.
